newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber closes mixed on adjustments.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber closes mixed on adjustments.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices were quoted mixed at the close on technical adjustments, following an absence of consumer demand, traders said.
"The market was quiet through the day, without any indication of buying interest," said a trader.
Dealers said supply of raw materials was still ample in the market, although production was somewhat affected by the wintering period which limits the flow of latex from rubber trees.
"Producers feel prices should not go below current levels, especially if supply is hit much later," said a trader.
At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted April RSS1 buyer at 305.50 cents ($1.23) a kg, up 1.50 cents from Monday.
April SMR 20 was one cent lower at 293.
Traders offered the SMR CV at 359, SMR L at 339, SMR 5 at 301, SMR 10 at 296 and SMR 20 at 294.
The INRO five-day average was 232.61 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on March 10 from 232.59 cents per kg on Mar 7. The daily indicator was at 233.07 against 231.97.
